summary: Fair first plays, soft night motes and the pier-aware follow camera are real, visible improvements; the 22:00 shot is readable and lit, with frame median ~2.6 ms (p95 3.9 ms). Two UI tests are still flaky in full-suite runs.

findings.what: Full-suite run is not stable: 'second E wave makes the creature follow' and 'Flower gift: flower still drawn after the gift' fail in alternating runs (48/49 twice, different failures). The author did not touch these this session, but the first-play fixes were closed as 'passes in the full suite' while the suite stays red.
findings.where: world/tests (Jump in wave, Flower gift), tests/reports/session-0029.json
findings.evidence: tester report: 48/49 at host run and again on re-run with a different failure
findings.suggestion: Print actions/goals in the check message and fix the underlying game choice (leave_interactions!, flower removal timing) rather than the test.
findings.response: Session 30: both flakes had causes. The wave: one E press both picked/gave a flower (flowergift.jl) and waved (greetings.jl), and the flower thanks 1.2 s later turned the new follower back into :answer. Now one key does one thing (flowergift uses_e/E_USED) and thanks never override :follow; the test waves from a flower-free spot. The gift: other critters pick flowers by themselves, so 'no flower drawn' was wrong; the test now checks one drawn flower per carrier. Also nightglow hid picked blooms only at night (test failed by day): fixed. Full suite re-run in session 30, see the journal.

findings.what: Evening lighting todo #118 was closed on luminance numbers, but the sky is still a flat navy/blue-grey with no real gradient or clouds, and the jagged grey horizon band in the raster is unresolved (two attempts reverted, new todo).
findings.evidence: 22:53 eye-level shot: sky is a near-uniform dark blue with dot stars; the moon-tint question from s28 was not rechecked
findings.suggestion: Keep the sky gradient/horizon issue as an open todo rather than counting #118 as fully done; add a sky gradient in the raster.
findings.response: Not this session: the sky gradient/clouds and the horizon band stay open as their own todo (lighting); session 30 went to creatures (weakest-but-one score) and the flaky suite.

findings.what: Pier-follow fix (#132) is verified by one before/after screenshot and a synthetic obstruction() value; no check across several creatures/poses, and obstruction() runs every frame in the follow camera.
findings.evidence: author: obstruction=4.0 live; frame p95 3.09 ms
findings.suggestion: Sample a few pier positions for the camera in a test, so later camera changes do not bring the planks back.
findings.response: Accepted; obstruction() costs are inside the frame budget (frame median 3.3 ms in session 30). A multi-creature check belongs to the camera director todo #119.
